comments.text_zh: 我认为这里的“简单”应该理解为“易于使用”。打个粗略的比方，自动挡汽车背后的机械原理并不简单，但它所提供的抽象让驾驶变得容易学得多。一个更有数学根基的例子是复平面与实数的对比：初次接触时，它在任何意义上都不简单，但它为许多（原本是实值的）问题提供了简洁的解法（也许是因为它在代数上是封闭的？）。注：这个库的作者还做过一个非常有趣的几何代数演讲（以这个库为演示载体），是 SIGGRAPH 2019 的：[视频]。这个之前已经在 HN 上被发过几次了。
comments.text: I think that simple should be understood here as easy to use . As a crude analogy, the mechanical principles underlying a car with an automatic shift aren't simple, but the abstraction it provides makes driving much easier to learn. A more mathematically grounded example could be the complex plane compared to the real line: when encountered for the first time, it is not simple in any way, but it offers a clean solution to many (originally real valued) problems (perhaps by the fact that it is algebraically closed?). NB: the author of this library also made a very interesting presentation of geometric algebra (using this library as vehicle) for SIGGRAPH 2019: [VIDEO] It has been posted a few times on HN before.

comments.why_zh: 解释了几何代数为何优于矩阵、向量、复数
comments.quote_zh: 他在 SIGGRAPH 2019 有一个很好的视频
comments.text_zh: 嗯，我最近正痴迷于几何代数（又称 Clifford 代数），然后偶然发现了 ganja.js [1]。它是一个无依赖的单文件，而且……令人印象深刻。未压缩 120k，用它你可以构造任意阶的代数（包括那些更冷门的双曲／抛物型代数），还能渲染到 canvas、svg 甚至 webgl（！）。它还包含一个巧妙的小型 DSL 解析器和解释器（它重载了科学计数法来命名基向量！），让你可以用各种乘积从简单的东西构造出更复杂的东西。作者 Steven De Keninck 也相当厉害，他早年在 demoscene 起步。他在 SIGGRAPH 2019 有一个很好的视频 [2]，解释了为什么这种代数优于［矩阵、张量、向量、复数］。特别让我感兴趣的是二维射影几何。我不想过度吹捧，但 ganja 真他妈棒，我有太多想用它做的事。首先，我想用它把我的物理学位课程重新过一遍。[1] [链接] [2] [视频]
comments.text: Well I've been on a real Geometric Algebra (aka Clifford Algebra) kick lately, and ran across ganja.js [1]. It's a single no deps file that is...impressive. 120k uncompressed, and with it you can construct any degree algebra (including the more esoteric hyperbolic/parabolic ones), render to canvas, svg or webgl(!). It also includes a clever little DSL parser and interpreter (it overloads the scientific notation to name basis vectors!) that lets you construct more complex things from simple things using various kinds of products. The author, Steven De Keninck, is quite impressive as well, having got his start in the demoscene some time ago. He has a good video from SIGGRAPH 2019 [2] that explains why this algebra is better than [matrices, tensors, vectors, complex numbers]. Of particular interest (to me anyway) is the 2D projective geometry. I don't want to oversell it, but ganja is fucking amazing and there is a great deal I want to do with it. For one, I'd like to recapitulate my physics degree with it. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: > 说得直白点，这一切听起来像是在用一条绕来绕去的路重新发明欧几里得几何。我的意思是，把仿射变换的一个子集（缩放、平移、旋转）应用到正交坐标系上已经能给你这些东西了，这一切究竟还能多给你什么？它确实是在试图重新发明欧几里得几何。但我不觉得它绕。举个最典型的例子，就拿我们正在评论的这篇文章来说：插值旋转。或者更一般地说：插值变换。仅仅是用旋转做这件事而不遭受 gimbal lock，就已经把你带到四元数了。四元数“绕”吗？所有对象都原生属于这个代数，这意味着它们可组合。比如这张幻灯片里，4D torus 的坐标公式和 4D PGA 中的公式：[LINK] 这个演讲总体上有一堆示例应用：[VIDEO] 诸如“这条线和这个平面的交点”“过两点的直线”“这两个球面相交处的圆”“三个平面的交点”“这条线在这个平面上的投影”之类的问题，在几何代数里都是平凡的、原生的（结果对象是代数的一部分）且无异常。例如，两个平面总是相交，只不过如果它们平行，交线就是一条无穷远处的线。用来把一个点绕原点平移和旋转的完全相同的代码，也可以用来把一条线或一个平面绕原点平移和旋转。Al
comments.text: > Quite bluntly, this all sounds like an attempt to reinvent euclidean geometry following a convoluted way. I mean, what does all this buy you that applying a subset of affine transformations (scaling, translation, rotation) to an orthogonal coordinate system doesn't give you already? It is attempting to reinvent Euclidean geometry, yes. I don't think it's convoluted though. To give a prime example, take the article we're commenting on: interpolating rotations. Or more generally: interpolating transformations. Just doing this with rotations without suffering gimbal locks already brings you to quaternions. Are quaternions 'convoluted'? The fact that all objects are native to the algebra means they're composable. Take for example this slide of the formula of a 4D torus in coordinates, and in 4D PGA: [LINK] The talk in general has a bunch of example applications: [VIDEO] Questions such as "the intersection of this line and this plane", "the line through two points" "the circle where these two spheres intersect", "the point at the intersection of three planes", "the projection of this line on this plane" and such are trivial, native (the resulting object is part of the algebra) and exception-free in geometric algebra. E.g. two planes always intersect, it just happens that the intersection is a line at infinity if they're parallel. The exact same code used to translate and rotate a point around the origin can be used to translate and rotate a line, or a plane around the origin. Al

comments.author: jiggawatts
comments.story_title: Why is Maxwell's theory so hard to understand? (2007) [pdf]
comments.text_zh: Maxwell 的理论之所以难懂，是因为它建立在一个差不多合适、但并不完全合适的代数之上。就像 stringly-typed 编程一样。它能用，但很乱、很难理解。Maxwell 那组耦合的微分矢量电磁方程，在几何代数里会简化成一个短得滑稽的单一方程。随手在 Google 上搜到这篇比较经典电磁学和 GA 表述的论文。这甚至还不是最简单的表示，因为最简单的表示用自然单位和 4D GA，基本把整套电磁理论压缩成大约相当于 4 个字符的方程，而且天然就是完全相对论性的：[LINK] 这几乎像个笑话。对我来说，这让人想起看初学者写程序。你会看到他们干出各种疯狂的事，比如要算“下个月”的日期，就把格式化好的日期字符串拆开、解析出月份，意识到日号有时候是一位数有时候是两位数，然后还得操心 m-d-y 还是 d-m-y 格式，建一堆“每月天数”和闰年的小表格……诸如此类。他们能写出好几页毫无错误的代码，但它仍然是错的，因为正确的做法就是直接调用“thedatevar.AddMonth(1);”然后完事。PS：3D 游戏引擎的矢量代数库在这一点上和物理数学完全一样。比如叉积很奇怪、必须选一个基、没法对旋转做插值、gimbal lock、舍入误差、2D 和 3D 要用不同的数学、还有一堆
comments.text: Maxwell's theory is hard to understand because it's based on an almost-but-not-quite-appropriate algebra. It's like stringly-typed programming. It works , but it's messy and hard to understand. Maxwell's set of coupled differential vector electromagnetic equations simplify to a hilariously short single equation in Geometric Algebra. A random Google turned up this paper comparing classic EM and the GA formulation. It's not even the simplest possible representation, because that uses natural units and a 4D GA to basically condense the entire set of EM theory into about 4 characters worth of equation that is fully relativistic for free: [LINK] It's almost a joke. To me it's reminiscent of looking at beginner programmers. You see them do crazy things like calculate a date "next month" by taking apart the pretty-printed date string, parsing to find the month, realising that sometimes the day part is one digit and sometimes it's two, then having to worry about m-d-y or d-m-y formats, building little tables of "days per month" and leap years... and so on. They can write pages and pages of error free code and it's still Wrong because the correct way is to just call "thedatevar.AddMonth(1);" and be done with it. PS: 3D game engine vector algebra libraries have all of this in common with the physics maths.
